items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: Marx, as I understand it, has some nineteenth century concepts

ctx.x: I think the jet plane, the computer, the chip, changed everything. It brought everything--that was the thing that tipped it over. It was already there but without the computer, there could be no jet airplanes. None of that stuff would be; television couldn't have satellites up there.

For all that technology and its purpose, why are we using it, and I think that question really has to be answered. Unfortunately we don't have any thinkers in the avant garde there, who have been prepared for this; Marx certainly wasn't. Marx, as I understand it, has some nineteenth century concepts; if there are parts of it that

work today, great; but essentially it's a nineteenth century concept. It is always laisse faire. Neither of them really worked and I'm suppose to answer an article on folk music here and the guy says, put it into Soviet constitution that they should preserve these folk ways, it's very important, but that's one of the reasons Russia has built a wall around itself, that's true.
